Greater Vancouver Woodturners Guild
130th chapter of the
American Association of Woodturners
Newsletter Vol. 2 Issue 11 – Special Edition
August 2001
We are moving to a new location!
Art Liestman
Just a reminder that beginning September 26th,
our regular (fourth Wednesday of the month)
meetings will be held at the Sapperton Pensioners
Hall at 318 Keary in New Westminster. To get
there from Highway 1, take the Brunette exit to
the south. Turn west on Braid (first stoplight) and
then turn south on Columbia. Keary is the street
on the south side of the Royal Columbian
Hospital. The Hall is just west of Columbia on
Keary.
Annual membership dues are payable at the
September meeting. If you can’t attend, we
would greatly appreciate receiving your dues by
mail. Please send your cheque for $30 payable to
the Greater Vancouver Woodturners Guild, c/o
Don Hoskins, 3676 Kelly Road, Belcarra, BC,
V3H 4R4.
Why are we here?
Art Liestman
To me, one of the main benefits of belonging to
our guild is that we can get exposure to worldrenowned woodturners who give demonstrations
and teach hands-on classes. We’ve had several
such visitors during the past year and will be
doing more in the years to come. I’d like to
encourage you to participate in these events.
The demonstrations are always educational, fun,
informative, and sometimes even provocative. I
always learn at least a couple of things that make
the expense worthwhile. Members at all skill
levels can benefit from seeing the demos.
Even more valuable are the hands-on classes. I
have found that in these classes you can make
major improvements in your turning skills in a
very short period of time. A good instructor can
make a huge difference in your turning. Each
instructor has different skills and ideas to share
with us. Don’t let these opportunities go by!
Don Derry Demo and Classes
Art Liestman
Don Derry of Ellensburg, Washington will visit us
September 15th – 18th for a demonstration and
two different classes. Please note that this is
BEFORE the September meeting!
Don Derry has been a woodworker for the past 35
years, concentrating on woodturning since 1994.
He spent several years doing the craft fair circuit
producing pen and pencil sets, turned boxes and
earrings. During that time, the bread and butter
product of his line was Christmas ornaments. He
sold almost 500 ornaments per year. In 1999, he
quit doing craft fairs to focus on artistic studio
wood turning. He is now known for turning large
state-of-the-art hollow forms of wood that are
brightly colored and polished to such a high
optical luster that they are often mistaken to be
fine art glass. Interestingly, the wood turning
techniques that he learned doing Christmas
ornaments have served him well as an artist.
Saturday, September 15th Demo:
This six-hour demonstration consists of a broad
group of techniques exhibited with wit, humor,
and philosophy. The day begins with a
demonstration of how to turn a very delicate and
extremely lightweight traditional style ornament
with the lathe going backwards and tools so big
that it will surprise even the most seasoned turner.
Don has a broad-minded approach to the craft of
woodturning and feels that no single turner’s
approach or turning technique is correct for
everybody. He proves this by showing and
explaining how he discovered that by using

objective self-observation, and asking oneself the
proper questions, a person may be lead to answers
and techniques that are often contrary to
established tradition. Don will then show how
turning a small hollow ornament ball is no
different than turning the gigantic artistic hollow
forms for which he is gaining a worldwide
reputation. He will demonstrate the state-of-theart torque arresting hollowing tools he has
developed and show that they are so easy to use
that anyone can learn the techniques and become
a master hollow form turner. Don will also
exhibit a way to prepare a shear scraper that is so
sharp you may never need sandpaper again.
Throughout the day, between flying wood chips
and entertaining banter, Don will be expressing
his unique point of view on the art world and what
is needed for the craft of woodturning to blend
seamlessly within it and why this is absolutely
necessary for the health and longevity of our craft.
There will be a $25 per person fee to attend the
demo which will begin at 9:30 am at Sapperton
Pensioners Hall, 318 Keary, New Westminster.
Sunday and Monday, September 16th and 17th -
“Sharpening the Eye” class:
This is a two-day hands-on class that will focus on
the decision-making process used by woodturners.
We will analyze, explore, and learn many ways to
be objective about our own work. We will begin
by turning a sphere between centers using only
the eye as a guide. The day will then progress by
turning models of many other basic forms. We
will explore egg forms, pear shapes, and cones on
the first day. The second day will be an
exploration of how these basic forms can be used
as the building blocks of more complicated forms
and integrated into almost any turning endeavor
that can be imagined.
Upon completion of the course, participants will
have a much better understanding of how their
own creative decision making process works and
how to use it to more easily produce works in
their own studios. Participants will also have
produced eight to ten form study models that they
can refer to in the future.
There is a $250 per participant charge for this
class.
Tuesday, September 18t h - Christmas
ornaments class:
This is a one-day hands-on course on producing
the traditional style turned wood Christmas
ornament consisting of a hollow globe with a
decorative top finial and a matching long icicle
bottom. The first half-day consists of an
introduction to the techniques for hollowing the
globe using a reverse lathe rotation technique and
a special hollowing tool supplied by the
instructor. The tools and techniques can be easily
learned and adapted to the more traditional
counter clockwise lathe rotation. The second half
day will be used for developing the spindle
turning techniques needed to turn a long and
delicate decorative icicle that will match the top
finial which covers the access holes that were
used for hollowing the small globe.
There is a charge of $125 per participant for this
class.
Requirements: Both classes begin at 9:30 am at
KMS Tools in Coquitlam. For both classes,
participants should have reasonable experience
with a roughing gouge and a half-inch spindle
gouge. Minimal experience with a skew chisel is
also helpful but is not necessary. Students should
bring a 1-inch or larger roughing gouge, a halfinch spindle gouge, and a parting tool and are
encouraged to bring any other tools that may help
adapt their personal style. The instructor will
supply any special tools required.
Sign Up Now! We have some spaces left in both
classes, but if you think you may be interested in
them, please let me know as soon as possible to
ensure a space! Call me at 604-939-3843 or email
art@sfu.ca.
